01 / The story so far

From studying systems
to building solutions.

I started in public administration, learning to ask how institutions, services, and incentives affect everyday life. At Sun Yat-sen University and now as a master’s student at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, that interest grew into a habit of looking past assumptions and asking what people actually need.

Adapt to China began as a question: how could everyday life in China become less complicated for people arriving from elsewhere? I founded and continue to operate the platform as a small, focused independent venture combining AI assistance with hands-on human support.

I handle product development, understanding user needs, communication, and service delivery. The work ranges from housing search and rental assistance to pet care, reservations and bookings, Chinese-language phone calls, and practical guidance on everyday life in China. With 5,000+ Instagram views and real service requests, the project has taught me that useful products are defined by whether they help someone complete the next step.

More recently, at YBBE TECH, I have been bringing that hands-on approach into enterprise software. I work across product discovery, AI-assisted development, and workflow prototyping: understanding client needs, turning ambiguous requirements into product specifications, and building and testing software that teams can evaluate and improve.

Collaborating across product, engineering, and business functions, I work on research and laboratory workflow prototypes such as AbTrace and explore meeting intelligence and document-processing workflows. These are prototypes that teams can evaluate before production deployment. The experience has made me more attentive to clear requirements, technical constraints, human review, system reliability, and communication across roles.
